name: Light Grey Blue
lede: Light Grey Blue is a pale, muted shade of [[grey-blue]], filed by the ISCC-NBS in 1955 and again by the xkcd crowd survey in 2010.

sections.title: A modifier on grey-blue
sections.body: The name is the modifier *light* applied to the base color [[grey-blue]], raising its value without changing its hue [1]. Our library's earliest record is the ISCC-NBS 1955 Circular 553, block 185, which calls the matching range "very pale blue," a Delta-E of 7.5 from this hex [1]. The xkcd 2010 survey records the same compound name independently, from crowd labeling rather than a standards body [1]. The nearest colors on file are [[pale-cerulean]] and [[cloudy-blue]], each about 3 units away, with [[light-king-s-blue]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 160 of 23,781 paintings, 0.67 percent; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 109 of them, more common than 60 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.8 percent of that century's 1,674 paintings, 1.4 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, by lightness rank, in half of its 109 appearances [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1474 work attributed to Piero della Francesca, 481 years before the name's first documented record in 1955 [2]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first; a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a dye [2].
